findings.title: canView(ClientModel) short-circuits via canView(), bypassing client-specific negative permissions
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client)`, calling `canView()` at the start evaluates `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` against only the `"Clients"` (all-clients) resource and immediately returns `true` if that succeeds, without ever calling `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` on the specific `client`. Unlike V1 where `canView()` only checked `canViewClientDefault()` (realm-management admin roles), in V2 an administrator can grant `view` on all clients via the `"Clients"` resource and define a negative permission denying `view` on a specific client (analogous to `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewUserPermission`). Because `canView()` evaluates only the `"Clients"` resource, `canView(client)` returns `true` even for a client with an explicit negative `view` permission. `canView(ClientModel)` should check `canViewClientDefault()` (like `canManage(ClientModel)` checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)`) and let `hasPermission(client, ...)` evaluate the client resource or fall back to the `"Clients"` resource.

findings.title: canView() returns false when caller has MANAGE or CONFIGURE permission on all clients
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` and does not consider `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (or `CONFIGURE`). In the parent class `ClientPermissions`, `canList()`, `canViewClientScopes()`, `canListClientScopes()`, and `requireView()` all delegate to `canView()`. Consequently, an admin granted only the `manage` scope on all clients will have `canManage() == true`, `canManageClientScopes() == true`, `canView(ClientModel) == true`, and `canView(ClientScopeModel) == true`, but `canView()`, `canList()`, `canViewClientScopes()`, and `canListClientScopes()` will all return `false`.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission queries resources by type that is not set on per-client resources and ignores transitive scopes
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` calls `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and checks `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`. This has three problems: (1) `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates per-client resources via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` without calling `resource.setType(resourceType)`, so individual client resources have a `null` type and are never found by `findByType`; (2) the all-clients resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` does have type `"Clients"` and name `"Clients"`, so `granted.add(resource.getName())` adds the literal string `"Clients"` instead of client UUIDs; and (3) `hasGrantedPermission` only checks exact scope equality (`scope.equals(s)`), so a caller with `manage` or `configure` permission on a client will not match when `getClientsWithPermission("view")` is queried.

findings.title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName does not resolve resource names for Clients resource type
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only handles `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` (returning `"All users"` or the user's username) and was not updated for `CLIENTS`. When a policy has resource type `"Clients"`, `getResourceName` falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (which is `null`), instead of returning `"All clients"` for the `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` resource or `client.getClientId()` for an individual client resource.

findings.title: Incorrect Javadoc on requireView() and requireViewClientScopes()
findings.body: The Javadoc comments added for `void requireView()` (line 96) and `void requireViewClientScopes()` (line 101) state `Returns {@code true} if ... returns {@code true}`, but both methods return `void` and throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `canView*()` check returns `false`.
